destinations.name: Rishikesh
destinations.shortDescription: River views, rafting, yoga, forest roads and weekend-friendly drives from Delhi NCR.
destinations.tagline: Where the Ganga leaves the mountains
destinations.overview:
Rishikesh sits where the Ganga runs out of the Himalayan foothills and onto the plains, and the town grew up along both banks around that meeting point. Most visitors split their time between the older ashram quarter near Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula and the quieter stretches upstream, where the river is lined with rafting camps and white-sand beaches.

Mornings are the best time to walk the ghats: the light is soft, the crowds are thin and you can watch the evening aarti preparations begin at Parmarth Niketan and Triveni Ghat later in the day. Cafes along the Tapovan side cater to long stays, and many travellers come for a week of yoga classes rather than a sightseeing checklist.

For a road trip, Rishikesh works well as a first night out of Delhi or as a base for day drives to Kunjapuri, Neer Garh waterfall and the forest road towards Neelkanth. Rafting runs from the stretches above Shivpuri when the river is calm enough; operators close during the peak monsoon for safety.

The town is largely vegetarian and alcohol is not sold in the main area, which gives it a calmer pace than most weekend destinations. Plan for traffic on Friday evenings and Sunday afternoons on the Haridwar road.

howToReach.summary: About 240 km via Meerut and Haridwar. Leave early to avoid weekend traffic around Haridwar.

faqs.question: Is Rishikesh good for a weekend trip from Delhi?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is about 240 km by road, so a Friday-night or early Saturday start gives you two relaxed days by the river.

faqs.question: When is river rafting open?
faqs.answer: Rafting generally runs from around September or October until June and pauses during the peak monsoon. Operators confirm dates each season.

faqs.question: Can I get non-vegetarian food or alcohol?
faqs.answer: The main town is largely vegetarian and alcohol is not sold there. Some stays outside the central area have their own policies.

faqs.question: Which side of the river should I stay on?
faqs.answer: Tapovan and Laxman Jhula suit cafe-hoppers and long stays; the Ram Jhula side is closer to the ashrams and evening aarti; upstream camps suit rafting trips.

destinations.name: Jibhi
destinations.shortDescription: A quiet Himachal valley base for Jalori Pass, Serolsar Lake, forest walks and slow cafe evenings.
destinations.tagline: Wooden homestays in the Tirthan side valleys
destinations.overview:
Jibhi is a small village in the Banjar valley of Kullu district, strung along a stream under pine and deodar forest. Traditional wood-and-stone houses have been turned into homestays, and the pace is slow: most days are a walk to a waterfall, a drive up to Jalori Pass, and a long evening on a balcony.

It makes a calmer alternative to Manali for travellers who want the Himalaya without the crowds. The road up from the Aut tunnel is narrow and winding, so plan to arrive in daylight, and expect patchy mobile signal in the higher hamlets.

Jalori Pass is the main day trip, with an easy forest trail to Serolsar Lake on one side and a steeper path to the ruins of Raghupur Fort on the other. Chehni Kothi, an old tower temple a short hike from Shringa Rishi, is another half-day outing.

Winter brings snow to the pass and sometimes closes it; the monsoon brings landslides to the approach road. Spring and autumn are the easiest times to visit.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: March to June, October to November

howToReach.summary: A long drive via Chandigarh, Mandi and the Aut tunnel; most travellers split it or leave before dawn. The last stretch from Banjar is narrow.

The nearest airport, with limited flights; continue by taxi via the Aut tunnel.

faqs.question: Is the road to Jibhi safe for self-drive?
faqs.answer: Yes for confident hill drivers in daylight. The road after Banjar is narrow with blind bends, so drive slowly and avoid arriving after dark.

faqs.question: Can I visit Jalori Pass in winter?
faqs.answer: Often, but snow can close the pass for days at a time. Check locally before setting out.

faqs.question: Is there mobile network and internet?
faqs.answer: Major networks work in Jibhi itself, but coverage is weak in higher hamlets and on the pass. Many homestays offer Wi-Fi.

faqs.question: How many days do I need?
faqs.answer: Three days lets you do Jalori Pass and Serolsar Lake, a waterfall walk and a slow day at the homestay.

destinations.name: Manali
destinations.shortDescription: Classic Himalayan hill town for snow, cafes in Old Manali, temple walks and drives towards Solang Valley.
destinations.tagline: The Beas valley’s busiest mountain town
destinations.overview:
Manali sits at the head of the Kullu valley on the Beas river, and has been a mountain holiday staple for decades. The town has two personalities: the busy Mall Road area with its hotels and markets, and Old Manali across the Manalsu stream, where guesthouses and cafes spill down a hillside of apple orchards.

The Hadimba Devi temple, in a cedar grove above town, is the classic first stop. From there most itineraries head north to Solang Valley for paragliding in summer and snow play in winter, and, road and permits allowing, on through the Atal Tunnel towards Sissu and Lahaul.

Manali is also a gateway rather than an end point: it is where the road to Leh begins, and a common base for treks in the Pir Panjal range. Traffic and parking are the main frustrations in peak season, so plan short drives early in the day.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: March to June, September to November

faqs.question: When can I see snow in Manali?
faqs.answer: Snow is most likely from December to February in town, and higher up around Solang Valley from late autumn to spring.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for the Atal Tunnel and Lahaul?
faqs.answer: Rules change by season and destination. Check the Himachal Pradesh government portal before travelling beyond Solang.

faqs.question: Old Manali or Mall Road?
faqs.answer: Old Manali suits cafe-hopping and quieter stays; Mall Road is convenient for families, shopping and transport.

faqs.question: How many days do I need?
faqs.answer: Three days covers the town and Solang Valley; add days for Sissu, a trek or a slower pace.

destinations.name: Mussoorie
destinations.shortDescription: Colonial-era hill station above Dehradun with ridge walks, Himalayan viewpoints and an easy drive from Delhi.
destinations.tagline: Ridge walks above the Doon valley
destinations.overview:
Mussoorie spreads along a ridge above Dehradun, with the Doon valley on one side and, on clear days, a line of snow peaks on the other. It became a hill retreat in the 19th century and still has the feel of one: long promenades, old churches, schools and bakeries, and cottages tucked into the oak forest.

The Mall Road links Library Chowk and Picture Palace and is the centre of town life in the evenings. Landour, a short uphill walk away, is quieter, with forest lanes, a clock tower and some of the best Himalayan views from Lal Tibba.

Mussoorie is one of the easiest hill stations to reach from Delhi by road, which also makes it busy on long weekends. Visit midweek if you can, and use Kempty Falls and George Everest's House as short excursions rather than full days.
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: March to June, September to November
destinations.seoTitle: Mussoorie Travel Guide: Places, Best Time, Weekend from Delhi
destinations.seoDescription: Plan a Mussoorie weekend: Mall Road and Landour walks, Lal Tibba viewpoint, Kempty Falls, the best months to go and how to drive up from Delhi.

howToReach.summary: Drive to Dehradun on the Delhi–Dehradun route, then climb the hill road to Mussoorie.
Dehradun is the nearest railhead with direct trains from Delhi; taxis and buses cover the climb.
The nearest airport, on the far side of Dehradun from the Mussoorie road.

faqs.question: Is Mussoorie good for a weekend from Delhi?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is one of the most practical hill-station weekends from Delhi by road. Avoid long weekends if you dislike crowds.

faqs.question: Mussoorie or Landour: where should I stay?
faqs.answer: Stay near the Mall for convenience and restaurants; stay in Landour for quiet forest walks and views.

faqs.question: Does it snow in Mussoorie?
faqs.answer: Light snowfall happens some winters, usually in January or February, but it is not guaranteed.

faqs.question: Is parking difficult?
faqs.answer: Yes, in peak season. Park once and walk: the Mall and Landour are best explored on foot.

destinations.name: Jaipur
destinations.shortDescription: The Pink City: hilltop forts, palace museums, bazaars and a winter-friendly drive from Delhi.
destinations.tagline: Forts, palaces and bazaars of the Pink City
destinations.overview:
Jaipur was laid out in the 18th century as a planned city, and its old walled centre, painted a terracotta pink, still follows that grid of wide market streets. The Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Jantar Mantar observatory sit within a short walk of each other, which makes the old city an easy first day on foot.

The great forts ring the hills to the north and east. Amber Fort is the most visited and is best seen early, before the day's heat and crowds; Nahargarh, on the ridge above the city, is the classic spot for sunset views over Jaipur.

Jaipur is also a shopping city, known for block-printed textiles, blue pottery and gemstones in the bazaars around Johari and Bapu. The winter months are pleasant; summer afternoons are very hot, so plan indoor museums for the middle of the day.

faqs.question: How many days do I need in Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Two full days cover the old city and Amber Fort; a third day allows Nahargarh, museums and shopping without rushing.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Amber Fort?
faqs.answer: Go early in the morning, soon after opening, to avoid heat and the largest crowds.

faqs.question: Is Jaipur good to visit in summer?
faqs.answer: It is possible but very hot. Plan sightseeing for early morning and evening and stay indoors at midday.

faqs.question: Is there a composite ticket for monuments?
faqs.answer: Rajasthan tourism has offered composite tickets covering several monuments; check current options at the first site you visit.

destinations.name: Udaipur
destinations.shortDescription: Lake city of palaces, ghats and rooftop sunsets, with day trips into the Aravalli hills.
destinations.tagline: Palaces on the water in Mewar
destinations.overview:
Udaipur grew up around a chain of artificial lakes, and the water still defines the city: the City Palace rises straight from the shore of Lake Pichola, island palaces float in the middle, and the old town's lanes tumble down to bathing ghats.

A boat ride on Pichola at sunset and an evening on a rooftop overlooking the lake are the city's signature experiences. The City Palace museum rewards a slow morning, while Saheliyon-ki-Bari and Fateh Sagar Lake make an easy afternoon loop to the north.

The surrounding Aravalli hills are full of day trips, from the Monsoon Palace on its hilltop to Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur further out. Udaipur is lovely in winter, and the monsoon, when the lakes fill, has its own appeal.
destinations.seoTitle: Udaipur Travel Guide: Lakes, Palaces, Best Time to Visit
destinations.seoDescription: Plan an Udaipur trip: City Palace, Lake Pichola boat rides, Fateh Sagar, the Monsoon Palace, when to go and how to reach.

howToReach.summary: Flights from major Indian cities; the airport is east of the city.
Direct trains from Delhi, Jaipur and other cities arrive at Udaipur City station.
Good highways connect Udaipur with Jaipur and Ahmedabad, making it a natural stop on a Rajasthan road trip.

faqs.question: How many days are enough for Udaipur?
faqs.answer: Two days cover the lakes and palaces; add a day for Kumbhalgarh or Ranakpur.

faqs.question: Is Udaipur worth visiting in the monsoon?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you enjoy green hills and full lakes. Expect some rain showers and humidity.

faqs.question: Where is the best sunset view?
faqs.answer: A boat on Lake Pichola, a lakeside rooftop, or the Monsoon Palace on its hilltop.

faqs.question: Is Udaipur good for couples?
faqs.answer: Very. Lakeside stays, boat rides and rooftop dinners make it one of India’s favourite couples’ destinations.
